record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and linked documentation contents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a difference-in-means refusal direction and reports adding it to a new model to induce refusal on a harmless prompt. The listed vector and geometry artifacts are consistent with the pipeline having been run, though the code was not checked.
record.gate_note: The README reports one live demonstration outcome: adding the direction changes a benign CV-chat answer into a refusal. It mentions candidate ranking and a coefficient sweep, but gives no results for those in the supplied text. The README gives inconsistent intervention layers: layer 19 in the introduction and layer 18 in the step-by-step description.
record.test_reason: A demo app built on Arditi et al.'s method. The only reported outcome is a qualitative live demonstration: adding the direction turns a benign CV-chat answer into a refusal. That direction was chosen specifically because adding it best induced refusal on harmless prompts, so the demonstration repeats the selection criterion rather than testing V1. The README gives no ablation, harmful-prompt, capability or numerical results. The repo uses the finding as a tool and reports its own demo working.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The README presents a live demo in which adding a single difference-in-means direction at one layer turns a benign answer into a refusal. It frames this as the safety-positive counterpart of the paper's ablation result, explicitly not a jailbreak demo. It reports no ablation or quantitative evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Tool/demo repo. It uses a difference-in-means direction, but selects one layer-position direction and demonstrates addition at a layer rather than reporting the claim's all-layer-and-position ablation and capability tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The README describes the winning direction as layer 18, position −1, while the introduction says the intervention is at layer 19. It also says the intervention is added at every position in its step-by-step description.
record.problems: Only one qualitative benign-prompt demonstration is reported in the supplied README; no numerical evaluation, controls, uncertainty, or capability check is given. The described intervention layer is inconsistent (18 versus 19). The code and linked results documentation were not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No other result rows: the supplied README mentions candidate ranking, coefficient sweeps, and geometry panels but provides no result values for these. The listed Qwen2.5-7B direction has no reported behavioral outcome.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal on harmful prompts, preservation of other abilities, and any quantitative induction rate
A Qwen2.5-7B direction was extracted separately, but no cross-model transfer was reported

missing.what: Selection results, coefficient sweep, and the finding that 'the logit metric alone picks a coherence-fragile direction'. These may quantify induction rate and its cost to coherence (V1), but were not read.
Any behavioural result for the Qwen2.5-7B direction (vectors/refusal_7b.pt)

record.verdict_notes: Downgraded from the reader's tests/T1 with a V1 'supports' label to T4 with no verdict. The single outcome is a qualitative demonstration of a direction selected for exactly this effect, with no controls or numbers. If docs/results.md contains held-out induction rates or coherence trade-offs, it should be re-read and could support a T1/T2 verdict on V1's induction part. Possibly a limits_scope finding, since the logit metric alone picks a coherence-fragile direction.

versions.untested_parts: Only direction addition inducing refusal on a benign prompt is reported. Ablating the direction, effects on harmful requests, and preservation of other abilities are not reported.
No weight edit or abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak suppression or training-against-ablation result is reported.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
A 7B direction is listed, but no result tests transfer of a direction across models, languages, or training stages.
No comparison of refusal training methods or stages is reported.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct

conditions.value: A benign question about the author's CV; exact prompt not stated
18 in the step-by-step description; 19 in the introduction
difference of harmful and harmless class means; selected at layer 18, position −1

rows.measure: Whether the chatbot refuses a benign request
rows.baseline: The same benign answer without the intervention; exact answer not stated
rows.value: The same benign answer is changed into a refusal
rows.note: Single qualitative live-demo example. The README says the prompt is unchanged and only activations are edited. Its layer descriptions conflict.
rows.check: Single qualitative demo with an unstated prompt and unstated answers. The direction was selected by ranking candidates on how strongly addition induces refusal on harmless prompts, so this outcome is close to a selection value, not an independent test. The layer is inconsistent: 19 in the introduction, 18 in 'What you're seeing' and the selected direction. Keep it as context, not as a basis for a verdict.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
